items.title: Somali Cabinet Approves Passport, Trade and Judicial Reforms
items.description: The council was briefed on Somalia's new third-generation electronic passport and was told that changes to personal data in issued passports have been stopped entirely to strengthen the document's credibility. Ministers also approved a Rules of Origin Bill allowing goods containing at least 30% Somali content to qualify for preferential treatment in regional markets. The law is aimed at boosting local production and exports following Somalia's entry into the East African Community and its participation in the African Continental Free Trade Area. items.titleIt: Somali Cabinet Approves Passport, Trade and Judicial Reforms

items.titleIt: Somalia Hosts Djibouti Police Delegation for Security Talks

items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. Ambassador Diene expressed appreciation for Djibouti's longstanding contribution to peace and security in Somalia, including the continued deployment of Djiboutian troops under AUSSOM. items.title: Somalia Says 25 Al-Shabaab Militants Killed, Four Surrender
items.description: The Ministry of Defence announced the outcome in a press statement released on Saturday, describing the operation as part of the Federal Government of Somalia's ongoing military campaign against Al-Shabaab. items.title: Ethiopia: Somali, Oromo Officials Discuss Cross-Border Challenges
items.description: The dialogue brought together officials from six districts in the Fafan and Sitti zones of the Somali Regional State and five districts from the East and West Hararghe zones of the Oromia National Regional State. items.title: Somalia Hosts Djibouti Police Delegation for Security Talks
items.description: During the visit, the delegation toured the Somali Police Force's Godir Special Police Unit, the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), the Counter-Terrorism Command, and the Haram'ad Special Police Command. items.title: Egypt: Egypt Sets 50 Percent Cash Collateral Limit in New Rules for Short Selling
items.description: [Daba Finance] Egypt has issued new rules for short selling on the Egyptian Exchange, requiring investors to provide cash collateral equal to at least 50% of the market value of borrowed securities. The Financial Regulatory Authority approved the framework under Resolution No. 155 of 2026 as part of efforts to increase trading and add more investment tools to the market.
items.titleIt: Egypt: Egypt Sets 50 Percent Cash Collateral Limit in New Rules for Short Selling

items.title: Drone strike wounds 13 in Tigray capital as fears of renewed war grow
items.description: A drone strike on Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia’s Tigray region, injured at least 13 people, including five children, a hospital official said Thursday. The attack comes amid growing tensions between federal and Tigrayan forces and fears the region could slide back into war.
items.titleIt: Drone strike wounds 13 in Tigray capital as fears of renewed war grow
